findings.observed: The root requiredBeforeFiling list includes all twelve count/charge/disposition cells in all four motion rows and all four proposed-order charge lines without a row-present condition. The shared motionFields function assigns unconditional SUPPLY to each row1..4. The guide enumerates every row as required completion. The exact official form supplies four available slots; it asks for actual counts, charges and dispositions of the case, not four mandatory records. A selected motion can have fewer than four actual rows even when the person's overall history meets the multiple-conviction route.
findings.correction: Condition required completion on an actual selected row. For an active row require its associated count, charge and disposition coherently; keep the proposed-order row associated with the same selected count. Spare rows must remain genuinely unused, not missing required facts, invented records or repeated copies of row1. Clarify this in participant instructions and the emitted map/blank evidence. Reuse the existing conditional-row vocabulary rather than inventing a new factory.
findings.testExpectation: Exercise one, two and four selected counts using distinct count/charge/disposition values; assert unused slots are blank/not-applicable and active rows remain complete. These are requested C regressions, not tests B claims to have executed.

findings.observed: DC-33 Part ThreeB's fourth statement expressly qualifies felony-to-misdemeanor reclassification with 'if applicable'. The map retains that wording, but the authored guide and assembled page10 impose a blanket do-not-file-until-advice instruction if a statement in the selected Part is not true, treating every unmarked statement as a gap. The guide does not distinguish this inapplicable statement from a false mandatory eligibility condition. The printed reclassification box is correctly left unmarked in these no-history fixtures; the defect is the added unconditional stopping instruction, not a fabricated checkbox observed in the PDFs.
findings.correction: Explain and represent conditional applicability explicitly. A person whose charge was always a misdemeanor must not be told they need a reclassification fact or new professional judgment merely because this conditional statement does not describe them. Leave it unmarked when inapplicable. Preserve stops for an actually false or uncertain mandatory condition, disputed reclassification, and the other genuine route limits. Do not change the official affidavit or pre-attest participant facts.
findings.testExpectation: Distinguish an originally-misdemeanor case, a supported reclassified case and an uncertain classification. An inapplicable box alone does not trigger the generic untrue-condition stop; uncertainty is not assumed away. No such participant-history tests are claimed executed by B.
